messages:
ellie_sales: Heads-up team — LumaTech POC planned to start Monday but procurement/legal raised blockers: (1) they require a signed orderform before any billing, (2) DPA contains an old subprocessor clause that looks permissive, (3) they want customer-managed HSM for keys, and (4) an EU subsidiary says final MSA must be wet-ink. Tagging @matt_legal @tina_procure @sam_se @viv_security @rev_billing.

matt_legal: Paste the DPA snippet pls. If it's the permissive-transfer language we usually propose either: A) notice + 30-day objection + SCCs; or B) named-subprocessor appendix requiring written consent. I'll draft both redlines.

ellie_sales: Their exact wording from counsel: "Vendor may engage legacy subprocessors and transfer Customer Data across borders without prior notice."

matt_legal: Can't accept as-is. I'll post concise redlines: (1) "Vendor will publish a subprocessor list, provide 30 days' notice of any changes and Customer may object; transfers subject to SCCs or equivalent safeguards." (2) "Named-subprocessor appendix with written consent required for additions."

tina_procure: On orderform: we can either block activation until PO/orderform signed or accept pre-paid credits (invoice on receipt) to start immediately. Finance default Net30; Net45 requires CRO approval. Recommend adding a modest overage cap (e.g., $1,500) to the orderform to avoid disputes.

sam_se: Hosted API does NOT support customer-managed HSM. Dedicated/Private do. If HSM is required for the POC we need Dedicated provisioning (lead time ~5-10 business days) and a price uplift (~20-30%). Short-term workaround: client-side encryption or scoped managed KMS, but procurement often rejects that.

viv_security: Request LumaTech complete our security questionnaire and share SOC2. Also ask the EU team to cite the policy that mandates wet-ink — many accept eSign with verifiable audit trail. Link: https://redwood.example.com/sec-qa

rev_billing: If they insist on no billing without signed orderform we need PO before activation. Pre-bill (Net0 invoice) unblocks immediately. If we accept eSign now and they later require wet-ink MSA, accounting will tag revenue as "POC - eSign limited" to prevent premature production recognition. We can also add a pre-authorized overage cap on the orderform.

ellie_sales: Proposed path for customer: 1) eSign orderform for POC with pre-billed credits (or PO) and $1.5k overage cap to start immediately; 2) customer completes security questionnaire + provides SOC2; 3) if HSM is non-negotiable we pause hosted POC and provision Dedicated (new orderform, lead time/cost uplift noted); 4) if EU sub requires wet-ink for final MSA we offer wet-ink for final MSA but request eSign for POC orderform to avoid blocking kickoff.

matt_legal: I'll attach the two redline options in a separate email/thread but paste short versions here so you can forward. Also adding an "eSign-limited" fallback clause to the orderform to protect us during the pilot.

docusign-bot: Created envelope ENV-555432 for LumaTech POC orderform (expires in 10 days). Signers: LumaTech PO, ellie_sales. Status: pending.

ellie_sales: Thanks — I'll send redlines + questionnaire to their counsel and ask for the EU wet-ink policy excerpt and billing contact. Will update this thread when they reply. :thumbsup:
